_note: The MyThuso shop. Devices, consumables and wellness goods a household buys between visits — and nothing else. Read directly by apps/web; generated into Swift and Kotlin by scripts/emit-shop.mjs. Prices are indicative rands from the funding proposal's retail line, not trading results. Delivery zones are not restated here: they are the coverage areas in packages/catalog/geography.json, so a suburb dispatch cannot reach is a suburb this shop cannot deliver to, by the same arithmetic. Dates are day offsets from today so the preview never goes stale.
_lawNote: Two Acts decide the shape of this file. The Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965 makes selling or supplying a medicine an activity for a licensed pharmacy holding a prescription where one is required — so no medicine is listed here at all, scheduled or not, and `neverSold` is enforced by scripts/check-boundaries.mjs rather than trusted. Section 18A of the same Act prohibits supplying a medicine according to any bonus, rebate or incentive scheme; packages/catalog/rewards.json therefore earns and redeems nothing against anything in this file that is a medicine, which is trivially true because there is nothing in this file that is a medicine, and stays true because the check fails the build if one ever appears. The Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008 is why a listing states what a thing does and never what it treats.

_productNote: `does` is what the object physically does. There is no `treats` field and no `claims` field, and adding one is a build error rather than a review comment — a shop listing is the single easiest place in this product to make a medical claim by accident, because the sentence that sells a thing and the sentence that claims it cures something are one word apart.

_neverSoldNote: Not a disclaimer. scripts/check-boundaries.mjs reads this list, and fails the build if any product's name, id or `does` sentence matches one of these words, if any product declares a schedule, or if any id in this file also appears in packages/catalog/dispensing.json. The shop cannot grow into a pharmacy by increments.

orderStates.name: Basket
orderStates.meaning: Chosen, not committed. Nothing is reserved and nothing is owed.

orderStates.name: Stock held
orderStates.meaning: The items are held for this household. In a real service this is where payment would begin; here it is where it stops.

orderStates.name: Quoted
orderStates.meaning: What it would cost, in writing, including delivery. No card is charged.

orderStates.name: Cancelled
orderStates.meaning: Released back to stock. Any points that were held are returned unspent.

delivery._feeNote: One fee, one threshold, both stated before a basket is opened. A delivery fee that appears at the last step is how a shop makes a person agree to something they did not choose.

refusals.sentence: We do not sell medicine here. A medicine reaches you through a pharmacy that has seen a prescription, not through a shop.
refusals.why: Supplying medicine is a licensed activity under the Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965. A shop that sells a monitor today and a painkiller tomorrow has become a pharmacy without a licence, and the step between the two is small enough to take by accident.

refusals.sentence: This is a preview. No card is charged, no order is placed and nothing is delivered.
refusals.why: Nothing in this repository is a real service. A shop is the screen a person is most likely to mistake for one, because shops are the thing they have used most often online.

refusals.sentence: This tells you what the item does. It does not say what it will do for you — a nurse or a doctor decides that.
refusals.why: A listing that says a device manages a condition has made a medical claim to somebody with that condition, alone, at night, with a card in their hand.

refusals.sentence: This device takes a reading. It does not tell you what the reading means, and a reading on its own is not a diagnosis.
refusals.why: A person who buys an oximeter because a screen implied it would tell them whether they are ill will act on a number nobody has interpreted. Every product that produces a number carries this sentence.

refusals.sentence: We cannot deliver to this address yet. It is outside the areas MyThuso reaches, and we would rather say so than take the order.
refusals.why: Delivery is held to the same coverage areas as a home visit. A shop that quietly accepts an order it cannot fulfil has sold a person a wait.

refusals.sentence: Someone else reserved the last one while this basket was open. It is no longer held for you.
refusals.why: Stock reserved twice is stock sold twice. The refusal is at the moment of reserving, not at the moment of delivering, because that is the moment a person can still choose something else.

refusals.sentence: This account belongs to someone under eighteen. A guardian has to place the order.
refusals.why: A minor may hold a health record here under a guardian. Holding a record is not the same as entering a sale, and conflating the two would let a child commit a household to a cost.
